description: Lead times for long-lead data centre equipment in the Indian market. Long-lead gear usually drives RFS (DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE.md section 4), so these numbers land directly on the critical path.
provenance_summary: INDUSTRY ESTIMATES, NOT PROJECT ACTUALS. Every figure is a defensible typical value for the Indian data-centre market, chosen to be in the right range and argued for in each entry's note. None is drawn from a vendor quotation, a purchase order, or a delivered project. Because lead time drives RFS, a wrong number here silently produces a wrong completion date that looks fully researched - so these remain unverified, assert_usable_in_live_plan() refuses them, and reasoning that rests on them is confidence-capped and flagged Tier-2. Decision point dp.long_lead_unconfirmed exists to stop the simulator using them unchallenged. Replace with real procurement data.
units: calendar weeks, ex-works to site delivery

entries.notes: Commonly cited as the single most frequent RFS driver. CRGO steel and copper supply, type testing and utility spec approval all extend it.

provenance.note: Indian domestic transformer manufacturing is comparatively strong (CG Power, Bharat Bijlee, TBEA, Toshiba T&D), so 33/11kV units run shorter than the 40-60 week figure often quoted for Western markets. CRGO steel is import-dependent and type testing plus utility spec approval extend the tail.
